newsitem.title: INDONESIA: JAKARTA STOCKS END DOWN DESPITE RATES CUT.
newsitem.headline: JAKARTA STOCKS END DOWN DESPITE RATES CUT.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended the week losing some 6.4 percent as the central bank's move to ease tight rupiah supply failed to boost sentiment on Friday, brokers and analysts said.
The Jakarta composite index was down 2.50 points, or 0.37 percent, to close at 675.44 points. Decliners led advancers by 70 to 47 with 69 issues unchanged.
Total turn-over was estimated at 604 billion rupiah.

"It (the central bank's move) briefly boosted sentiment, but the market lost momentum later as worries over a liquidity squeeze haunted the market again," Goei Siauw Hong, an analyst with Socgen Crosby Securities, said.
Indonesia's central bank, Bank Indonesia, cut rates on its short-term certificates (SBIs) for periods of one week and above by 50 basis points while maintaining high rates for shorter-term papers.
The bank for example cut seven-day bilateral SBIs to 9.5 percent from 10.0 percent, but it maintained high overnight bilateral SBIs at 14.0 percent and four-to-six day at 15.0 percent.
Brokers said the rates cut briefly boosted sentiment and prompted buying in selected blue chips particularly in the banking sector.
"The buying did not last long as it was mostly carried out by local investors, while their foreign counterparts remained mostly on the sidelines," one broker said.
Brokers said worries over high overnight SBI rates, new margin finance regulations limiting local retail client leverage and a slew of rights issues still remained.
"It (the market) is likely to remain weak.. as the overnight rates are still high," Robert Allison, head of sales with Paribas Asia Equity, said.
Among the losers were blue chips BII, Indosat and Indocement. -- Jakarta newsroom
